bodies.DRE-3602:
**Observed live 2026-09-11 08:17–08:24 PT, during the** [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) **walk.** `release_rows()` (`console/backend/release_row.py`, read through `LiveGitHubReader` every 30 s from the operator's checkout at `e8aa0d2`) followed the hand-dispatched release run 34615231805 through `ci_green` (15:17:43Z), `cut` and `build` (15:18:05Z) and `roll_out` (15:19:21Z), version `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.41`, detail "the release train is cutting console". At 08:20:48 PT a second train run (34615560824, `workflow_run` for the CI of the next merge) was created; from that tick the row switched to it — `stage: cut · mark: unk · "the release job for console has not started"` — while run 34615231805 went on to roll out, verify and land (`released … as agent-bureau-console-v1.6.41 at f041b10`, 15:23:07Z; tag `deployed: 15:23:03Z`). The row never showed `verify` or `live` for the release, and after landing it read `ci_green · hold · held_by: spacing · version: null` (the second run's no-op). The same masking happened at 07:41–07:47 PT: two runs fired three seconds apart for v1.6.40, and the row settled on the second run's "console reads current" with no version.

So the two things a person most wants from the row — "did it land?" and "what version is live?" — are exactly what a following run erases. [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s acceptance criterion 1 (an answer at each of CI_GREEN, CUT, BUILD, ROLL_OUT, VERIFY, LIVE) is unreachable whenever any CI completes within the ~6 minutes a release takes, which is most of the time.

## What to build

The row should follow the newest run **that is releasing or has released**, not the newest run of any kind. A run whose decision is `no-op`/`hold` (current, spacing, window, held, ci-pending) must not displace a release run that is still in flight or that landed more recently than the hold was decided; the hold's own sentence can ride as a secondary line ("next release may be cut at 08:53 PT") beneath the landed release's `live · v1.6.41`. `version` on a hold row that follows a release carries the landed tag, never null.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a release run in flight and a later no-op run created, `release_rows()` keeps serving the release run's stages through `verify` and `live` (a test drives the two-run fixture from this morning's run ids and times)
- [ ] After the release lands, the row reads `live` with `version` equal to the tag cut, and the later hold's sentence is served beside it, not instead of it
- [ ] A hold run with no release in flight still renders as today (`held_by` + the train's sentence)
- [ ] The bogus `${{ matrix.surface }}` row (already named in [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s record) is dropped from the served rows, or a separate card is filed for it and referenced here
- [ ] The parity test against bureau-pipeline@stable stays green

**Related:** [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) (the proof this blocked), [DRE-3336](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3336/epic-the-release-run-is-a-fact-the-console-can-read-release-acts-with) (the epic), [DRE-3524](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3524/console-release-rowpy-walks-the-inner-stages-off-the-deployment-record) (the record half of the row source).
bodies.DRE-3857:
agent-bureau's console, website and relay surfaces write their Linear releases through the release train's shared step (bureau-pipeline `scripts/release_linear.py`, [DRE-3854](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3854/the-release-train-writes-a-linear-release-for-every-surface-whose)) instead of each surface script calling agent-bureau's `scripts/linear_release.py`.

## Why

Once the train writes a Linear release for any surface that declares a pipeline, agent-bureau is the one repo still doing it inside its own scripts — a second implementation of the same rule. Filed as a follow-up and NOT built with [DRE-3854](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3854/the-release-train-writes-a-linear-release-for-every-surface-whose), so the shared step is proven on Portico first.

## To decide before building

* The console uses a pipeline access key and a two-phase cut (sync + `Deploying` before the rollout, complete after the tag). The train can only write after the tag. Moving the console loses its merged-not-live window; decide whether that is acceptable or the console stays on its script.

bodies.DRE-4054:
The store's card reads are `SELECT *`. Every one of them carries the full Linear description — a mean of **3.3 KB per row** — across the wire and into Python, several times per page load, for views that never render a description.

Found while measuring [DRE-4053](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4053/database-optimization-every-one-river-view-stops-re-deriving-the-same) and deliberately left alone there. After that card's work the One River page is 182 ms cold (64 ms database, 118 ms Python), and what remains of NeedsYou, AlertFeed and ActivityFeed — 10 to 14 ms of database time each — is largely this fetch plus event bodies. On a 1,884-card board the broad `state IN (...)` reads move roughly **6.3 MB of description** that nothing asks for.

It was left out of [DRE-4053](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4053/database-optimization-every-one-river-view-stops-re-deriving-the-same) for a real reason: the store methods that return these rows have callers well beyond the river, so narrowing the column list is not a local change. That is what makes it its own card rather than a line in that one.

**Blocked by:** [DRE-4053](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4053/database-optimization-every-one-river-view-stops-re-deriving-the-same) — its payload-parity gate is what makes this safe to attempt at all.

## Why this is now a safe change to make

`console/backend/tests/test_oneriver_payload_parity.py` executes all eleven One River documents against a deterministically seeded, production-shaped board and hashes every response against digests captured before any optimisation. A column that turns out to be needed after all shows up as a failing digest naming the view, rather than as a blank field somebody notices in production. Do not re-capture the goldens to make a change pass.

## Approach

Audit which callers of the card-returning store methods actually read the description, then either narrow the shared read or give the views that do not need it their own projection. Prefer one narrow read plus an explicit fetch for the few places that render a description over adding a second near-identical method — two readers of one row shape is how they drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The card reads on the One River path no longer select the description column where no consumer of that read renders it.
- [ ] Every call site of any store method whose shape changes is audited and updated — named in the pull request, not summarised as "all callers".
- [ ] `test_oneriver_payload_parity.py` passes with the goldens untouched, and `git log -- console/backend/tests/golden/oneriver_payloads.json` still shows only the commit that created them.
- [ ] `console/backend/bench/bench_oneriver.py` shows the database column falling, with before-and-after numbers per view in the pull request body.
- [ ] The full backend suite passes with nothing weakened, skipped or deleted.
- [ ] Any view that DOES render a description still renders it — pinned by a test, not by inspection.

## Reproducing the reading

```
<venv>/bin/python console/backend/bench/bench_oneriver.py
```

The db column is the one this card moves.

In Progress.title: The release row source yields a bogus second row for a train run with nothing to release — GitHub reports the skipped matrix job as `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}`, and the row reads `surface: "${{ matrix.surface }}" · unk`
In Progress.description:
**Repo:** agent-bureau

## What happened

Running the merged `console/backend/release_row.py` (`release_rows` with `LiveGitHubReader`) against the live train runs on 2026-09-10 06:50 PT (the [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the) proof, PR [dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau#2437](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/review/docsdre-3527-the-release-row-read-off-live-github-the-held-train-2b855d02ad90)) produced, beside the real `console · hold · window` row, a second row with `surface: "${{ matrix.surface }}"` and `mark: unk`. When a train run has nothing to release, GitHub never expands the matrix, and the skipped job is reported with its name literally as `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}`. The row source treats that job name as a surface. A CEO reading the Activity tab would see a release row for a surface called `${{ matrix.surface }}`.

## What to build

* `release_row.py` recognises an unexpanded matrix job (`${{` in the job name, or the job's `conclusion == "skipped"` with no steps) as "no surface released on this run" and yields no row for it — the real row for the run (the `hold` at `ci_green` with the rule that held it) already says what happened.
* Test-first: a fixture from the live run's jobs payload (the skipped `call / Release ${{ matrix.surface }}` job beside the plan job) yields exactly one row; a fixture with an expanded `call / Release console` job yields the console row.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No row ever carries a surface containing `${{`; pinned by the fixture.
- [ ] A held/no-op train run yields exactly one row, the hold at `ci_green`.
- [ ] PROOF: the next held train run read through the deployed console shows one row (recorded on [DRE-3527](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3527/proof-a-hand-dispatched-console-release-read-end-to-end-off-the)'s proof record).

## Not in this card

* The train's matrix itself — [DRE-3164](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3164/epic-the-release-train-one-reusable-train-in-bureau-pipeline-a-thin); reading the skipped job is the console's job.

In Progress.title: [EPIC] agent-bureau: label definitions, relations with ids, people and bots, projects, cycles, initiatives and all 14 workflow states get tables of their own and stay current
In Progress.description:
The things Linear holds beside the card get tables of their own and stay current: label definitions with their ids and groups, relations in both directions and of every type with their relation ids, people and bot identities, Linear projects, cycles, initiatives, and all 14 workflow states including the two nobody has ever entered. Today the record contract indexes only `Issue` and `Comment` deliveries; every other Linear type (`IssueLabel`, `IssueRelation`, `Project`, `Cycle`, `Initiative`, ...) is saved to S3 and applied to nothing, relations live only as a JSON blob the poll writes, labels exist only as names on a card and as a repo file, and there is no table for users, projects or cycles at all. This child widens the contract so those deliveries are indexed and applied, adds the tables, and names a poll with a stated maximum age for the one thing Linear sends no delivery for (people). It is the gap table's rows 6, 7, 9, 18, 20, 21, 22 and 26, held current.

**Why it is cut here, after DRE-6059.** This child owns the record contract's indexed-event list — `LINEAR_INDEXED_EVENTS` in `config/record-contract.json`, mirrored byte for byte into `cloud/relay/record_contract.py`, `cloud/relay-gh/record_contract.py`, `cloud/record-jobs/record_contract.py` and `console/backend/record_contract.py` by `make sync-mirrors` — plus a new applier module beside `linear_record.py` for the non-card types, new DDL + alembic tables (`linear_workflow_state` from alembic 0081 is the pattern: platform-level, no tenant), the matching store methods, and the people poll in `console/backend/poller.py`. It waits on DRE-6059 because both add alembic revisions to one chain, both add store methods to `store.py`, and both touch the dispatch in `linear_record.apply_linear_envelope`; and because DRE-6059 stores actor ids, label ids and relation targets exactly as the payload carries them, so the tables here name what it already holds rather than the two inventing the shape twice. The planner of this child confirms, from the relay's live Linear webhook subscription, which of these types already arrive; any type that does not is one operator step (a checkbox in Linear's webhook settings) filed as its own card, not a build.

**Rows 23 and 24 are the CEO's decision, asked once by this child's planner, with its plan — and the approval answers it.** Attachments (mostly PR links, which GitHub already gives us) and Linear Releases (which `record_release*` already derives from GitHub deployments) are the two rows the parent names as likely "deliberately not held". The planner puts one plain question in front of the CEO alongside this child's plan, with its recommendation: deliberately not held, both rows. A comment from him on this epic is the answer. Moving this epic to In Progress without one is also an answer: the plan he approved carries that default, so from the approval's time both rows read deliberately not held, and nothing in this epic waits on him for it. The proof card quotes whichever applies, and the fourth child's parity check records both rows as a decision with the decision named — never as a gap, and never as undecided.

**Not in this child.** No change to how an Issue or Comment payload is applied (DRE-6059). No backfill of label, relation, project, cycle or user history for anything written before this ships, and no re-application of the IssueLabel and IssueRelation deliveries already sitting in S3 — the third child does that, through the Record's own backfill walk. No parity change (the fourth). No search. Nothing here moves a write off Linear.

**Reference, do not rebuild:** `config/linear-workspace.json` and `make linear-apply` (workspace-as-code, row 26, stays the repo file that writes Linear; the tables here are what Linear says back), DRE-5731 (blockers past twenty), the `linear_workflow_state` table.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An `IssueLabel`, `IssueRelation`, `Project`, `Cycle` and `Initiative` delivery is indexed in `event_record` under the contract's Linear key and applied to its table, and the four contract mirrors stay byte-identical under the existing parity test.
- [ ] Label definitions are held with Linear's id, name and group for every label in the workspace, and a card's labels resolve to those ids (row 6).
- [ ] Every relation on a card is held with its relation id, type and both ends, in both directions, and a relation created or deleted in Linear reaches the table through its delivery, not only through the 15-minute poll (row 7).
- [ ] All 14 workflow states are held with id, name, type and team, including In Design Review and In QA, read from Linear's workflow-state list and not only from the states cards have entered (row 9).
- [ ] People and bot identities — at least the CEO, agent-bureau, qa-bot, sandbox and agent-bureau1 — are held with Linear's id, name and whether each is a bot — `kind`, exactly `user` or `app`, one vocabulary whichever feeder wrote the row — kept current by a named poll whose maximum age is stated in the code and on this epic (row 18).
- [ ] Linear projects, initiatives and cycles are held with their ids, names and the cards in each — a project's and a cycle's directly, an initiative's through its projects, which is how Linear holds them — and a card's project and cycle are readable off our database (rows 20, 21, 22).
- [ ] The CEO's decision on attachments and Linear Releases (rows 23, 24) is recorded as held or as deliberately not held, with the decision named: by his comment on this epic, or by his approval of the plan that carries the default (deliberately not held, both rows), with the PT time of whichever it was.
- [ ] The child's own PROOF card observes, in production, one label edit, one relation added and removed, one project change and one cycle change arriving through their deliveries and landing in the new tables, recorded with PT times.

**Blocked by:** DRE-6059

In Progress.title: [EPIC] agent-bureau: the backfills — every issue Linear ever held, every comment's id and author, the full history, and the side tables — run in production and counted
In Progress.description:
**Split on 2026-10-07 at the first critic's send-back.** The seam reader named the history run (DRE-6099) and the comment identity run (DRE-6101) as waiting on observing the missing-issues walk run live (DRE-6095), and the same critic found the roster run (DRE-6094) unordered against that walk. A card on the far side of a watched run is a second epic, not a later step (`standards/card-quality.md`, DRE-3244), so those three are canceled here with their replacements named — DRE-6106, DRE-6107 and DRE-6108 under DRE-6105, each blocked on this epic's PROOF card — and DRE-6105 is blocked on this epic. Relation ids for relations that predate the Record, which no card here can read because the Record never held them, are DRE-6105's too.

**Why it is cut here, after DRE-6059 and DRE-6061.** The backfills write into columns and tables those two children declare, so they cannot be written before the shape exists. More than that, what each backfill must select is measured, not assumed: the first two children run in production for a while and the gap each leaves (a card the path has not touched since it shipped, a comment written before August) is what the selection reads off the live database — the pattern of `console/backend/linear_created_backfill.py` (select the NULLs, write only into a NULL), `console/backend/approved_at_backfill.py` and `console/backend/comment_thread_backfill.py` (run in-VPC through `make console-task`). Two sources feed them, and the planner chooses per row: the Record itself, walked with `console/backend/record_backfill.py`'s `TASKS` pattern for the IssueLabel and IssueRelation deliveries and the old Issue payloads already in S3, which costs no Linear call; and Linear, read by identifier through `linear_quota.post` under a named operation, for what the Record never held — archived and deleted issues, issue history (`issue.history` with from-state, to-state, actor, label and priority changes), old comments' ids and authors, and the user, project, cycle and label lists. This child owns the new `*_backfill.py` modules, their store selection and fill methods, the two card columns that hold Linear's archive fact and their one alembic revision (DRE-6090), the `TASKS` entries in `record_backfill.py`, the search read (a backend query over our own `card` and `event` rows, not a Linear call), and one `OPERATOR` card per production run it makes.

**One lane rule, and the archive fact held as data (second critic and operator pre-review, 2026-10-07).** The walk (DRE-6090) gives an archived or trashed card the lane the live path gives a leaver — `poller._gone_from_linear`, the rule DRE-5702 decided and DRE-6076 keeps — and that rule answers `Archived` or `Deleted` only for a card whose Linear lane is still a board lane; a finished card (Done, Canceled, Duplicate) keeps its finished lane, because `Archived` and `Deleted` are outside `TERMINAL_STATES` and moving it there would un-finish it for its blockers, its epic's done count and DRE-6078's finish times. The rule is not changed and no card here edits `poller.py`. Linear keeps the archive beside the workflow state, not in it, so the archive and trash facts go to two new card columns DRE-6090 adds, `card.archived_at` and `card.trashed`, stamped on every card Linear answers archived or trashed, board lane or finished. So the 281 held cards from the 2026-10-05 removal that show Done or Canceled keep that lane and gain `archived_at`, which closes gap row 13's "no `archived_at`", and most of the removed cards the walk newly stores land in a finished lane with the stamp. The walk's summary counts `finished` and `stamped`, and the operator's record (DRE-6095) and the proof say how many of each. No card here writes a second lane rule.

**Every fill reaches every stored card, routed or unrouted (second critic, 2026-10-07).** The walk stores a card naming no repo unrouted, as the console keeps such cards, and the DRE-0xxx to DRE-1xxx range is mostly such cards. The roster, history and comment identity selections (DRE-6089, DRE-6093, DRE-6098) read every stored card, routed and unrouted alike, through the store's existing opt-in (`include_unrouted=True`), and the proof counts the same set with the unrouted share stated beside each number, so every baseline it records is a count those runs can clear. The comment identity selection is the NULLs alone — a card whose thread is marked whole is selected all the same when a comment on it lacks an id, an author or an author kind, because the mark proves the thread complete and nothing about identity. The routed-only reading of the existing `linear_created_at` backfill is that one column's own reason (an unrouted card always carries it) and not a convention the new fills copy.

**Labels by id are the roster fill's (second critic, third round, 2026-10-07).** DRE-6061 keeps a card's labels by id in a table of their own, `linear_issue_label`, fed today only by an `Issue` delivery (DRE-6083's `apply_issue_sides`) and the 15-minute board poll (DRE-6085's `record_poll_nodes`), which reads board lanes alone, so a finished, archived or deleted card no delivery has touched since DRE-6059 shipped never gets its rows from either. The roster fill (DRE-6089) reads `labels { nodes { id name } }` and writes the ids through `linear_side_store.replace_issue_labels` with the node's `updatedAt`, in the same act as the placement row, so row 5 is filled by id as well as by name. A label-less card has no row legitimately, so the fill's third selection test is the cards whose `labels_raw` names a label and whose `linear_id` has no row, and that is the baseline the proof records for DRE-6106; a card whose `labels_raw` still names labels Linear has since removed is kept selected by design and counted under `labels now none`.

**One other card edits the console-task allowlist, and it is ordered after ours (second critic, third round, 2026-10-07).** DRE-6070, under the parity epic DRE-6064 (in Planning), edits the same four launcher files as DRE-6088 to add `linear_parity_full`, and both cards pin the allowlist tuple.
